rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran with no truncation; 10 blocking findings survive, chiefly that the k8s v4 exec has no stdin half-close so the response write in tool_call_channel.py hangs (AC1 still pending-stage-7 manual proof), plus a failing standards security row. Reachability stayed unconfirmed for the session-close race (CR-005) and the non-timeout kill gap (CR-004), so confidence is medium; 0 deferred (no deferred file written) and 24 candidates dismissed as handled by the guard, below the emission floor or out of scope.

standards_review.notes: All 8 subjects in the review range match the documented EPMCDME-####: Description format (EPMCDME-15401: ...)
Apache header and future annotations present; signatures typed with X | None and parameterized generics. Ruff and license-check were not run (read-only review).

security-patterns.md Untyped Input Handling forbids lossy repair before parsing; tool_call_channel.py:141 decodes script-written request bytes with utf-8 'replace' before json.loads. No secrets or shell interpolation found.

findings.title: OverflowError escapes parse_tool_calling_timeout
findings.problem: parse_tool_calling_timeout is documented as never raising, but float(raw_value) only catches ValueError. An integer too large for float (for example 10**400 written in the customer-config YAML) raises OverflowError.
findings.impact: A malformed timeoutSeconds fails the whole workspace script run instead of falling back to the 120 s default, contradicting the requirement that bad values never fail a run.
findings.recommendation: Catch (ValueError, OverflowError) around float(raw_value) so the value falls through to the warning and the default.

findings.title: Lock wait/hold log skipped on timeout and error
findings.problem: The tool_calling_run log with lock_wait and lock_hold is emitted only after _run_locked returns normally inside the with-lock block. A SandboxTimeoutError or any other exception skips it. The spec requires the log for every effective run.
findings.impact: The longest lock holds, which are timed-out or failed tool-calling runs, are the ones missing from the required observability, so pod-lock contention cannot be diagnosed from them.
findings.recommendation: Log in a finally block around _run_locked (or record the hold time in the exception paths) so every channel run emits lock_wait and lock_hold.

findings.title: Stale exchange folders swept only when channel exists
findings.problem: _run_locked returns straight to session.run when channel is None, and sweep() lives only on ToolCallChannel. Story AC9 requires leftovers of an interrupted run to be removed at the start of the next run in the same conversation. A next run with the switch or per-run flag off, or with the limit clamped off, never sweeps.
findings.impact: Exchange data from an interrupted run stays on the pod indefinitely once tool calling is no longer active for the conversation, so the 'not persisted' guarantee of AC9 is not met.
findings.recommendation: Sweep the bridge folder for every pooled workspace run (a module-level sweep helper that needs no channel), or make the runner build a sweep-only exec when tool calling is off.

findings.title: Non-timeout run errors leave script running
findings.problem: _run_locked calls cleanup(kill=True) only on SandboxTimeoutError. Any other exception from session.run (transport error, dropped websocket, closed session) goes through the finally with cleanup(kill=False), which deletes the exchange folder without killing the script. Reachability was not confirmed: whether the pod process survives a dropped exec depends on the runtime.
findings.impact: The script can keep running on the shared pod after the pod lock is released, overlapping the next run, with its exchange folder deleted underneath it. Reachability of the survive-on-disconnect case was unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Kill on any exception that escapes session.run (except Exception: channel.stop(); channel.cleanup(kill=True); killed = True; raise), keeping the non-kill cleanup for the success path only.

findings.title: Low-TTL check can close a session in use
findings.problem: The new min_remaining_seconds branch of _is_session_healthy calls _close_session under _pod_management_lock only, not the per-pod execution lock. _select_or_wait_for_pod picks a running pod at random when at capacity, so a second request can reach a pod whose session another thread is executing in. With the default 120 s limit the check fires for any session older than 120 s instead of the previous 300 s TTL. Reachability of the concurrent case was not confirmed.
findings.impact: An in-flight run (possibly a tool-calling run) can have its session closed underneath it. Reachability was unconfirmed, so this is capped at major.
findings.recommendation: Do not close or recreate a session whose per-pod lock is currently held (check _get_or_create_lock(pod_name).locked()); treat it as unavailable or pick another pod instead.

findings.title: Lossy UTF-8 replace on untrusted request bytes
findings.problem: _POLL_SCRIPT decodes each script-written req.<id>.json with data.decode('utf-8', 'replace') before the backend json.loads and dispatches on op. security-patterns.md (Untyped Input Handling) lists errors=replace as an anti-pattern for external input. KILL_SCRIPT line 188 reads the pid and start_time files with decode('ascii', 'replace') too, though that path fails closed.
findings.impact: The backend acts on data that was never actually sent, and a documented security standard is violated on a path fed by sandboxed, untrusted code.
findings.recommendation: Decode strictly in the poll script and report a bad-encoding marker on UnicodeDecodeError so _build_response answers bad_request; read pid/start_time strictly in KILL_SCRIPT and exit 0 on UnicodeDecodeError.

findings.title: Kill marker untested against sandbox prefix
findings.problem: SANDBOX_CMDLINE_MARKER is a hard-coded copy of llm_sandbox.SANDBOX_SYSTEM_FILE_PREFIX. The kill tests inject their own 'SANDBOX_*' cmdline literals, so nothing ties the marker to the real script filename.
findings.impact: If the prefix changes, KILL_SCRIPT silently exits 0 on the marker check and a timed-out script keeps running on the shared pod after the lock is released, with every test still green.
findings.recommendation: Import the prefix from llm_sandbox (or assert SANDBOX_CMDLINE_MARKER == SANDBOX_SYSTEM_FILE_PREFIX) and add a kill test that uses a cmdline built from the real sandbox file naming helper.

findings.title: write_stdin('') is not EOF; response cat hangs
findings.problem: KubernetesExecRunner.__call__ signals end of input with response.write_stdin(''). The installed kubernetes ws_client speaks only v4.channel.k8s.io, where write_channel sends an empty text frame on channel 0 and there is no stdin half-close. _WRITE_RESPONSE_SH is 'cat > "$1" && mv ...', so cat never sees EOF, the exec never closes, and the loop 'while response.is_open()' has no deadline. Bytes and str are also mixed across the two write_stdin calls.
findings.impact: No response file is ever published, so every echo call times out in the script; the channel thread blocks forever in _respond, is not stopped by stop() within its join, and leaks a cat process in the pod. The core feature (AC1) does not work on a real exec.
findings.recommendation: Do not depend on stdin EOF: pass the body with an explicit length (for example a python3 -c script reading exactly N bytes from stdin, or a base64 argument split across argv), and add an overall deadline to the exec read loop so a stalled exec is closed and reported as ExecFailed.

findings.title: Channel thread dies silently on failures
findings.problem: _run catches only ExecFailed and _build_response/_parse_request catch only TypeError/ValueError, so any other exception (for example RecursionError from json.loads on deeply nested request JSON, or a future handler error) kills the daemon thread with no response. After ExecFailed the thread returns for good without telling the script.
findings.impact: The script then waits out its full SDK call timeout (100 s) for every later call with no error response or marker, so a transient exec outage or one bad request breaks the rest of the run.
findings.recommendation: Catch Exception around handler dispatch and request parsing and answer with an error response; on persistent ExecFailed write a channel-unavailable error to pending requests or a marker file so the SDK fails fast.

findings.title: Cleanup retries fire without backoff
findings.problem: _exec waits between attempts with self._stop_event.wait(backoff * attempt), but cleanup() and its kill exec run after stop() has already set the event, so wait returns immediately and all attempts fire back to back.
findings.impact: The retry-with-backoff requirement is defeated in exactly the cleanup and kill path, so a transient failure there is unlikely to recover and the script or exchange folder may be left behind.
findings.recommendation: Use time.sleep (or a separate non-stop event) for cleanup backoff, or clear/skip the stop event in the housekeeping execs.
